title: CoT Omission Rate: Do Models Selectively Hide Concerning Steps?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct and critical: if models systematically omit concerning reasoning from CoT in sensitive contexts, this undermines the core premise of CoT monitoring. This finding would reshape how the safety community evaluates CoT-based control protocols.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires designing honeypot tasks with tempting shortcuts, running a reasoning model, and building a discrepancy detector between CoT and final action. DeepSeek-R1-8B is open-source. Honeypot task design requires creativity but is within CS student capability with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one model with sensitive vs. benign task comparison. But designing honeypot tasks and building a CoT-action discrepancy monitor are two non-trivial subtasks. Achievable in 30 hours with good task design upfront.
